title: MCMC receives complaint over AI-generated porn depicting students, teachers
key_facts: Malaysia's communications regulator (MCMC) confirmed on Thursday 8 Oct 2026 that it received a complaint about AI-made sexual images and videos allegedly of students and teachers at a school in Kedah.
Creating or distributing such content falls under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
The penalty is a fine of up to RM500,000 or up to two years in prison, or both; offences against children may carry up to five years.
Licensed platforms have child protection duties under Section 18 of the Online Safety Act 2025.
The Communications, Home and Education Ministries and police each have a role; MCMC will cooperate in the investigation.
MCMC urged the public not to create, upload or share such content.
quote_evidence: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) confirms it has received a complaint over the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) to create and distribute sexual images and videos, allegedly of students and teachers at a school in Kedah.
"If convicted, a fine of up to RM500,000 or imprisonment for up to two years, or both, may be imposed.
why_it_matters_hint: A regulator is treating AI-made sexual content about schoolchildren and teachers as a criminal matter.
